name: Geshem (the Arab)
title: Arab opponent of the rebuilding of Jerusalem
summary: Geshem was an Arab leader who, together with Sanballat and Tobiah, opposed Nehemiah and the Jews in their rebuilding of the walls of Jerusalem. He represented the Arab resistance to the Jewish restoration after the exile and tried to stop the work through threats, mockery, and intrigue.

keyEvents.title: Mocks the rebuilding project
keyEvents.description: Geshem joined Sanballat and Tobiah in mocking the Jews and accusing them of rebellion against the Persian king when they began to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: Spreads false rumors of rebellion
keyEvents.description: Geshem and his allies sent word to Nehemiah, claiming it was reported that the Jews were planning a rebellion and that Nehemiah intended to make himself king.

keyEvents.title: Tries to lure Nehemiah into a trap
keyEvents.description: Geshem took part in planning to lure Nehemiah to a meeting on the plain of Ono with the intent to harm him. Nehemiah saw through the plan and refused to come.

keyEvents.title: Fails to stop the wall building
keyEvents.description: Despite repeated attempts to stop the work through threats and intrigues, the Jews completed the wall in just 52 days, and Geshem's opposition was futile.
